text:
felix: hey folks, first-week kubeconfig weirdness. I had an existing ~/.kube/config from another job and `aws eks update-kubeconfig` merged entries. Now `kubectl config current-context` points to a context named `dev-cluster` but it's the old company cluster, not redwood-dev. How do I safely fix this without nuking my whole kubeconfig?

ria: welcome! two easy options: (1) set KUBECONFIG to only the redwood file when you run update (export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood:$KUBECONFIG), then `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` to re-merge cleanly; (2) use `kubectl config rename-context <old> <new>` or `kubectl config delete-context` for the stale one.

felix: i'm on WSL2 + Windows so my home kubeconfigs were weirdly split. Is there a safe way to inspect without changing anything?

julie: do `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/config.win kubectl config view --raw` to preview the merged output. You can also `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` to list names only and then `kubectl config use-context <name>` for the redwood one. If names collide, `kubectl config rename-context old-name redwood-old` then rename the redwood one to `dev-redwood`.

felix: thanks. one more: after I get the right context, will I still need an infra request for namespace access? `kubectl get pods -n felix-dev` returns Forbidden currently.

ria: yes, context fixes kubeconfig but RBAC is separate. File the k8s access form and request namespace `felix-dev` and role `onboard-edit`. Infra usually creates a RoleBinding in that namespace. After approval re-run `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` so the session maps to the new role.

infra-bot: access request created by felix at 2001234575  id K-33177. Assigned to infra oncall. ETA ~90 minutes.

julie: small WSL tip: symlink your Windows kube file into WSL (~/.kube/config -> /mnt/c/Users/You/.kube/config) so tools inside WSL and Windows apps see the same config. Also keep a backup: `cp ~/.kube/config ~/.kube/config.backup.$(date +%s)`.

felix: awesome — cleaned up contexts, re-ran `aws sso login`, filed the form. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n felix-dev` still says "no" until infra approves. will update when it's live. thx!
